findings.problem: The explanation for "Iconium" jokes "I'd need a nap and a glass of milk." Milk is a food or drink other than cookies, and it isn't in Acts 13:13-52.

rule.text: In jokes and comparisons, cookies are the only food he mentions.

findings.problem: The joke in the "jealousy" explanation doesn't make sense: "I couldn't get three bakers to a taste test, and even I wouldn't be jealous of THAT crowd. Okay, maybe a little." Someone who can't draw a crowd would be more likely to be jealous of a big one, not less, so "even I wouldn't be jealous" is backwards and leaves the reader asking "huh?"

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: Both explanations name Pilate (Acts 13:28) without saying who he is. This choice card comes before story card 11, and that card doesn't introduce him either, so this is the first time he shows up in the lesson.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The "Scoffers" explanation says "God says He's doing a work in their days," and the "Idol makers" and "False shepherds" explanations call it "God's work." Acts 13:40-41 only says this "was spoken by the prophets" and never names who the "I" is. Naming God as the speaker comes from Habakkuk 1:5, and no reference is given for it.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The "Back to Jerusalem" explanation ("one helper lighter") and the "Down to Joppa" explanation ("One helper peels off") call John a helper. Acts 13:13 doesn't call him that. The fact comes from Acts 13:5, and no reference is given.

rule.text: Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: The "prophet" explanation says "Asking for a prophet when Samuel's standing right there." Acts 13:20-21 says only that God gave judges "until the time of Samuel the prophet" and that the people then asked for a king. It doesn't say Samuel was there when they asked. That detail comes from 1 Samuel 8, and no reference is given.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The "sandals" explanation says untying sandals is "the lowest job there is" as a fact, not as a joke. Acts 13:25 says only that John is not worthy to untie the sandals. The "robe" explanation is softer ("about the humblest job around"), but it adds the same idea.

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: Nearly every explanation follows the same shape: the answer or a correction plus "friend", then the full verse in quotation marks with its reference, then one closing line. All of the explanations quote the verse, even where it adds nothing (for example, the three explanations on stop 1 card 6 and on stop 3 card 15 each quote the same full line). Most of the explanations for missed answers on the same card read as near copies of each other (stop 3 cards 4, 8, 15 and 17, and stop 2 card 8).

rule.text: There is no formula. Each explanation sounds natural and different from the others.

findings.problem: Many explanations have no humor at all and read as plain restatements, for example: stop 2 card 6 ("Saul's son Jonathan", "Samuel the prophet"), stop 2 card 16 ("Samuel the prophet of Israel", "Saul son of Kish from Benjamin"), stop 3 card 4 (all three), stop 3 card 8 (all three), stop 3 card 15 (all three), stop 2 card 2 ("False") and stop 2 card 4 ("temple").

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
